details:
Q1: Which merges should still count as "merged" for both the sweep's close and the workflow's `ai:merged` label? The same rule applies in both places, so the two stay consistent.
Choices:
A) Only merges into the repository's default branch, exactly as written. Orchestrator sub-issues and integration-branch follow-ups then stay open without `ai:merged` after their PRs merge.
B) Default-branch merges, plus `ai:orchestrator-managed` sub-issues merged into any branch. This keeps today's managed-child behaviour. Non-managed issues merged into any other branch (including a declared integration branch) stay open.
C) Default-branch merges, plus merges into the issue's own declared `Integration branch:` from its body metadata (this covers managed sub-issues and integration-branch security follow-ups). Any other base, such as the incident's #4748 merging into its own `claude/implement-plan-issue-4688-*` branch, stays open. The body is read by adding `body` to the existing `gh issue list --json` call, so there is no new API call. (RECOMMENDED)
Q2: When an issue's PR merges into a branch that does not qualify under Q1, what should happen to the issue afterwards?
Choices:
A) Leave its existing phase label (for example `ai:ready-to-merge`) and leave it open. Closing it is left to whatever later merges that branch into a qualifying branch; no new automation in this issue. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Same as A, and also make the sweep close the issue once the PR's base branch has itself been merged into the default branch. This adds a per-candidate compare call and widens scope.
C) Same as A, and also post a one-time comment on the issue saying the merge was into a non-target branch, so the issue does not look stuck.
